test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 19 July 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: In an election between two candidates, one got 60% of the total valid votes, and 10% of the votes were invalid. If the total number of votes cast were 10800, what was the number of valid votes for the other candidate?
solution:
Given:

Total votes is 10800

One candidate gets 60 percent of valid votes

10 percent votes are invalid

Concept:

Valid votes percent + invalid votes percent = 100%

If one candidate gets x percent valid votes other candidate should get (100 – x) percent valid votes.

Calculation:

Valid votes = 90% of 10800 = 9720

Votes other candidate gets = (100 – 60)% of 9720

⇒ 40% of 9720 = 3888

∴ The other candidate got 3888 votes.
